beats.text: Slept with your ex? It might not set you back.
In two studies, almost five hundred people who'd recently broken up reported on their lives, some of them every single day.
Trying to have sex with an ex did not slow down their recovery. Not day to day, and not two months later.
The people most eager to hook up were the ones still attached to their ex.
But even for them, it didn't bring more distress.
As the lead researcher put it: the hand-wringing may not be warranted.
So, no shame. Just be honest with yourself about why.

sources: Spielmann, Joel & Impett (2019). Pursuing sex with an ex: Does it hinder breakup recovery? Archives of Sexual Behavior 48 (online 2018). Study 1: 113 recently broken-up participants, daily diary + survey 2 months later; Study 2: 372 participants. Pursuing sex with an ex not associated with hindered recovery; more common among those still attached; not linked to more distress. Quote: 'societal handwringing regarding trying to have sex with an ex may not be warranted'. Via ScienceDaily 2018-10-17.
